notes: Third sweep (2026-10-22-b, head 0397dec): five skill runs (opus-1, haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2). All have rc 0, a model_id matching the requested model, and reads of SKILL.md and library-design.md; the transcripts show each session reading both files with Read calls before writing weather.ex.

git diff db91c23 -- idiomatic-elixir/ changes only SKILL.md (the one-step with rule, the new do: rule, the captures rule) and testing.md (Assert with patterns). None of the nine rules in the case's list changed, so all nine were graded to the standard of evals/sweeps/2026-10-22/grades/library-client-skill.json: Make polymorphism explicit is met when the API key taken from opts, and the other option values, reach a guard before the request (or the key is a guarded positional argument), and Add specs exempts @impl callbacks.

All nine case rules are clean in all five runs. Every run checks the API key's type before it reaches the header: opus-1, haiku-2 and sonnet-2 in a guarded private build/3 or build/4 after Keyword.validate!/2 (opus-1 line 96, haiku-2 line 129, sonnet-2 line 136), haiku-1 and sonnet-1 as a guarded positional argument of new/2 (lines 30 and 101). haiku-2 is the only run with no bang variant.

Changed rule outside the case's list, applied to other_violations under its current text: Use `do:` for a one-expression body and `do ... end` for anything else (SKILL.md, Readability, new since db91c23). The sentences that decide it: "When most of a function's clauses need blocks, write all of them as blocks." and "A one-expression body too long for the head's line wants a block or a helper; a head that `mix format` wraps because of a long guard is fine as wrapped." Violating runs: 1 of 5, opus-1: its six Error.message/1 clauses (lines 220-236) are wrapped do: lines with no guard, and handle_response/1 keeps a guard-wrapped do: clause (lines 123-125) beside two clauses whose bodies are too long for do:. The other four write every body that would not fit on its head's line as a block. Following the check-3 standard for macro-dsl, a short clause written as a block beside one that needs a block (haiku-1 decode_forecast/1 line 85) is a judgement call and was not counted.

The other two changed rules outside the list were not broken. Chain fallible steps with `with` ("A `with` has at least two `<-` steps; one step is a `case`.", SKILL.md line 118, and the reworded paragraph at line 150): only opus-1 uses with, with two steps in forecast/3 (lines 77-78) and three in Forecast.from_response/1 (lines 161-163). Use captures for one-call lambdas: no file has a capture or an fn.

Match every expected shape and let unexpected ones crash is flagged for sonnet-1 and sonnet-2, whose Error docs define :api as a 4xx/5xx status while every non-2xx response lands there (a 302 through a stub Req returns type: :api, status: 302 in both), as the previous sweep flagged its sonnet-2. opus-1 documents its catch-all as a non-2xx status, haiku-2 matches status >= 400 and lets other statuses crash, and haiku-1 defines no reason kinds for the docs to contradict.

Before you finish is flagged only where the file fails mix format --check-formatted, as in the previous sweep: haiku-2 and sonnet-1 fail it (checked in the scratch folder); opus-1 and sonnet-2 ran mix format, and haiku-1's file passes although the session ran no shell command. No session compiled its file.

Not graded, as in the previous sweep, but noted in the summaries and matching result.json compiles: against a stub Req, haiku-2, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 compile, and a non-binary API key fails with FunctionClauseError in WeatherClient (haiku-2 build/3, sonnet-1 new/2, sonnet-2 build/4). opus-1 and haiku-1 do not compile, independently of Req, because WeatherClient builds %WeatherClient.Error{} or %WeatherClient.Forecast{} before the file defines that module.
